question.worked_solution:
Isolating the exponential term, we find

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3{e}^{x}-{e}^{3/2}}{2\sqrt{e}} & >e \\ 3{e}^{x}-{e}^{3/2} & >2e\sqrt{e} \\ 3{e}^{x}-{e}^{3/2} & >2e\cdot {e}^{1/2} \\ 3{e}^{x}-{e}^{3/2} & >2{e}^{(1+\frac{1}{2})} \\ 3{e}^{x}-{e}^{3/2} & >2{e}^{3/2} \\ 3{e}^{x} & >3{e}^{3/2} \\ {e}^{x} & >{e}^{3/2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, taking the natural logarithm of both sides and applying the laws of logarithms, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{x}) & >\operatorname{ln}⁡({e}^{3/2}) \\ x & >\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
